blocks.text:
Role
Founding Product Designer

Timeline
December 2021–November 2025
[hero image: img.json]

Trigate is an integrated and scalable solution for delivering innovation services powered by TrigUp that helps Innovation Ecosystem Entities (IEEs), including accelerators, incubators, innovation institutions, venture capital firms, and science and technology parks, run programs, deliver education and coaching, manage startup applications, monitor their progress, and centralize documentation. Over time, the product evolved from a WordPress MVP into a white-label SaaS. Today, it serves over 6,000 startup users and 20+ IEEs across all 31 provinces of Iran.

Feedback and Strategic Pivot: Introducing the White-Label Premium Plan
As we demoed Trigate to a broader network of IEEs, we noticed a persistent pattern: several organizations expressed strong interest in the tool but hesitated to convert into paying customers. Since TrigUp aimed to scale the product into a robust, sustainable revenue stream, we needed to uncover the exact friction points preventing these interested prospects from buying.

blocks.text: Deep Dive 1 — Removing the drop-off

Not all users arrived at Trigate with the same intent. While some were founders prepared to register a company and apply for an accelerator program, others were team members joining an existing startup via an invitation code. A third group consisted of aspiring entrepreneurs who weren't ready to launch an idea but wanted to explore Trigate's free educational content and resources.

The Challenge: Comprehensive Documentation vs. Low Completion Rates

runs.text: The Challenge: Comprehensive Documentation vs. Low Completion Rates

blocks.text: Coaching is a fundamental support service that IEEs offer to accelerate startup growth. Coaches routinely meet with their assigned founders to provide strategic guidance across various business dimensions, including team, market strategy, and product development, while simultaneously assigning and tracking actionable tasks. Following each session, completing a progress report was mandatory for administrative logging. IEE management relied heavily on these reports to monitor how startup cohorts were progressing and to proactively identify vulnerable teams requiring additional intervention or resources.

The Problem: Moving Beyond a Basic User Directory
Early-stage founders often seek co-founders or core teammates to complement their skill sets, offset time constraints, or accelerate growth. However, discoverability is only half the battle. The deeper challenge lies in evaluating mutual alignment, determining whether a prospect truly fits the startup's needs, possesses verified credentials, and can evolve into a dependable, long-term collaborator.

The Platform Dilemma: Open vs. Gated Ecosystems
The benchmark revealed a clear industry trade-off:

The benchmark revealed a clear industry trade-off:

blocks.text: Open Ecosystems: Lowered the barrier to entry and accelerated initial user acquisition, but suffered from shallow profiles, weak filtering capabilities, and lower baseline trust.

runs.text: Lowered the barrier to entry and accelerated initial user acquisition, but suffered from shallow profiles, weak filtering capabilities, and lower baseline trust.

blocks.text: Because Trigate was still actively growing its network, neither path offered a viable standalone solution. Launching a gated matchmaking feature would provide robust filters but too few participants to generate meaningful matches. Conversely, making it entirely open might inflate sign-up metrics, but would dilute Trigate's vetted quality and damage match relevance.

blocks.text:
The Strategy: Sequencing "Pull" Before "Match"
To bypass this deadlock, I proposed a phased product roadmap: leverage Trigate's core value proposition to organically pull qualified participants onto the platform first, then deploy matchmaking as an exclusive, gated feature within that high-trust network.

This organic engagement naturally generated an initial layer of user context and qualification data before they ever entered the matchmaking funnel.

The Final Roadmap Sequence:
Deliver Core Value → Attract Vetted Users → Build Network Density → Apply Advanced Filters → Generate High-Relevance Matches

Based on these findings, I recommended prioritizing and launching Trigate’s core operational features first. This strategic postponement allowed us to establish the necessary audience baseline, ultimately ensuring a high-relevance, trustworthy matching experience at scale.
